correctness.rationale: For odd q, the norm/Capelli argument proves f_{a,b} irreducible iff χ(b)=χ(a²−4b)=−1; the t=4b/a² substitution is exactly two-to-one off a=0 and preserves all exceptional roots in the character indicator. The quadratic pair sums equal −χ(−1),−χ(−1),−1, and the triple sum is −a_q(E_u); this yields C=(q+1+a)/4. The diagonal follows from a squarefree quadratic sum. Double counting ordered distinct nonsquare constants establishes the aggregate in all q. The independent Frobenius-gcd verifier checks 2,788 parameter pairs over 11 finite fields but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: No directly equivalent all-odd-field exact multiplicative pair-correlation statement was located after multiple semantic searches, prior research records comparison, and inspection of closely related primary text. The contribution is a complete natural finite-field factorization-count classification and its associated aggregate; it is distinct from the known general Legendre point-count first moment, from asymptotic factorization results, and from quartic value-set identities. Classical reduction tools and character sums are acknowledged. The residual risk of an unlocated three-character-pattern specialization is substantive.
residual_risks: An old result on three simultaneous quadratic nonresidues or Jacobi character patterns may imply the formula after a nonobvious substitution; available literature coverage is not exhaustive.
Classical character sums make the proof elementary; novelty is in the complete ratio-conditioned paired-irreducibility classification, not new elliptic or quadratic-character machinery.
The 2003 author PDF has some pages not fully inspected owing to extraction limitations; conclusions about noncoverage rely on the inspected relevant sections and other full texts.

value.rationale: Counting simultaneous irreducibility for correlated sparse-polynomial pairs is a natural arithmetic distribution invariant. The complete parameter classification distinguishes impossible, diagonal, and elliptically correlated cases, yields uniform nonemptiness from Hasse, and determines a total exact multiplicative correlation. It is neither an isolated small-field enumeration nor a routine substitution into a previously identified paired-irreducibility formula.
